Epilogue ~Roy and Sabrine~
***Part 1: Empire City Before the Journey West***, as told to Gil, Warden of Waters

'Morning, Gil. How's things holding up for you? We've been setting up shelters for as many people displaced from Hampstead as we can. Most of them in the borough itself, but also some free of iron and silver in the park for people waiting on medical care. I've mostly been caring for people rather than physical work, but Kukudh's barely had a chance to rest with all the messages and deliveries - not that they'd admit they're tired. So whenever I can get a moment between making berries, stabilising people, just talking to people who need it - I've been helping them with heavier deliveries.'

'I ended up at Ferrytown one morning to pick up some enchanted blankets, but I got there a bit too early, so decided to sit under a tree and wait. Next thing I knew it was afternoon, one of the blankets was covering me, and the rest were in a box nearby. It was... heavier than I expected, but I managed to carry it back. Turns out - someone had put a lot of other supplies in with the blankets, with a note saying they were for the people of Hampstead. I don't know who it was, but they have our thanks.'

'Even once the rebuilding is complete, I'm hoping we can continue providing food and shelter for people who need it. With the two of us, we at least have some variety in berries if there's nothing else, and by the time we leave, we should have people able to help.'

"Hey, Gil. Hope you're doing well. Today we finished helping Secel and Jean-Paul with their house over in Hampstead. Good thing we started with some rudimentary cleanup of the borough and set up some huts and other shelters to the survivors first. Some of the people were there back when we were putting the money changer's place back up, and it seems that they remembered it. There is a spark of hope. People started helping one another. Some even offered to help us with Secel's and Jean-Paul's place."

Roy sighs.
"I was worried about it - after all, building a house for a few while the rest are getting temporary huts. But, looks like people decided that the place where their close ones rest needs caretakers. Anyway, the park will have new, trusted caretakers while we're traveling - Fuddles and Cairn decided to move here. I know the park will be in good hands. And it'll be fitting for the house for her family to be built upon the cornerstone she inscribed. We're starting drawing plans in a few days, we have some other things to do in the meantime.."

'Gil, I finally found an opportunity to go to the library... I know, you said it would be better to move on, and I agree - but I'd rather have made one last look for answers, so I can move forwards without the guilt of not trying to apologise. I looked into news, genealogy records, obituaries, and I found... not much. But enough that I know there's little point in searching further.'

'Lovlatar, first. Soon after I died, a lady named Crescens Lovlatar was found dead nearby. It ended up as a cold case, as she seemed to have no external injuries, and no valuables were taken from her besides a--- besides my hat and dress. With that, and that I could take her name... I doubt it was natural causes, as that would imply I had been travelling with her to know it. So my conclusion is that either the ***Thing*** killed her, or I did... All I can do now, though, is pray she's resting peacefully - it would likely cause more problems than it would solve to let people know...'

'As for Louhi. I... found my own obituary. Pretty strange thing to read, all things considered. I - and others - died to a British airship attack, which the news claims came from Hampstead. Although their only proof was me - I was being prepared for burial when I woke up. The Redcoat I remember throwing me out was one who just happened to be stationed there, who was worried about Hampstead's fog creeping into the village. Which I can understand.'
'I'm not going to look into it any more. I've done all I can, without digging too deep... at least, here. I'm... still thinking about the, ah, other thing...'

"Mornin', Gil. The plan's progressing nicely. Not only several people, probably more than necessary, donated their airships for the cause. Based on the prototype I built out of the Aphid, we definitely have enough resources."

"Oh yeah, Jigsaw's helping improve upon the initial design, using all the stuff they had in the workshop where Mal had his tank built. We got some folks from the old Blackthumb guild on it too. The prototype is already running, though on low gear, but I'll probably take it down in a few days to improve it. At least Edriata's happy with the initial findings."

'...alright, Gil. I made my decision. I'm... not going to try bringing back Katrine with the emergency resurrection you left us. As much as I want to... it wouldn't be fair to her, for a start. It's been so long, she's probably moved on - I wouldn't want to risk causing her pain by, as Kukudh puts it---'
`Yoinking her back into this material plane.`
'That, yes. Thanks, Kukudh. A-anyway. With how little I can remember, I doubt anything would be guaranteed to work without... a lot more research, that would throw me back into the past again. And trying with what I know now, and failing, would do the same thing. No - all I can do is live, and honour her memory. And who knows... perhaps she'll find her way to you somehow. If she does - please look after her as you did for me.'

"Hey, Gil. We've done it. Along the east side of the Hudson there's now about a dozen fully-functioning water-purifying stations. They should only need maintenance every once in a while, to replenish essence fuel, and replace the filters with clean ones. By our predictions, with the west side protected by Feytown's magic, it should take between a few months and a year to be absolutely sure we can consider the river clean. The magic others have provided will speed up the initial cleanup, but the stations will then be able to run in the future, and make sure the river stays that way."

"I hope that helps you as much as it'll help the city. I'll need to find people who'll keep the stations going while we're away. I have a few ideas already. Now I'm just thinking what I can do with all the spare parts. Don't worry, I'll figure something out. I'm not leaving any mess behind."

"Hi Gil. It's been a week or two since we last were here in the park. Our trip to the other states was pretty eventful. I thought we could still use the opportunity as sort of a test run of our road trip. The other states haven't been hit as much by the war as the City, and looks like despite their allegiance to the Union, many people there are either native, or well integrated."

"So... you might have more followers now. We invited those interested to visit us here at Murry Hill, they'll probably be here in a few days - we didn't want to pull anyone along by force. We should probably think of having someone here representing the interests of people beyond the Union's borders. With Tom here as well, it could become a workable embassy of sorts, I suppose. As long as Fuddles won't mind neighbors and we won't take too much of the park itself. Priorities are priorities. And you know, after this short trip, I think I have an idea what to do with all the leftover parts."

'Hey, Gil, you're likely already aware of at least some of this. But you know I've been looking for someone to keep an eye on the spiritual side of things here while we're away? I found someone I feel you'd approve of, an elf cleric named Ruto. He took refuge here with his friend Darunia, a tabaxi wildfire druid, a while ago. The two of them have been through some tough times even before the war started, they used to be pretty destructive, but they're trying their best to get their flames under control.'

'Darunia's not really religious, though Ruto told me that since they got here, he's been taking to thanking the souls of meat and fish he eats for the meal - Ruto, though, has been spiritual his whole life, although has been growing rather disillusioned lately due to worshipping a god of tempests. If he's willing, and you're willing, I would happily induct him as a cleric of peace under your guidance. Tonight, I'm going to take him to the pond, and fully explain the tenets, the meditation process, and the specifics of the role.'

"Evenin', Gil. Normally I would've done this as an end-of-day thing, but, well, we kinda got kept up in Feytown and ended up sleeping there. Sab says she felt kinda odd, but I didn't see much difference."

"Anyway, we went to chat with Ferrah and the shifter kids under her care. I wanted to ask them all about their plans, and suggested something for those undecided. You know how with my mostly being active at night and ending up doing support for those on the front line, and picking up some loose ends that needed doing, my values up from before just naturally aligned with your tenets? I was wondering if maybe the kids there would be interested in picking up some small errands that would help the city they live in. Especially that they're, well, they had to make a new family for themselves together. Give them the impression that they can make a difference, not just float wherever fate carries them."

"Darragh seems to be really on board, I think she'll be running things before we know it. As, well, my legacy of sorts, I suppose, I called this group of ours the Night Shifters. Yes, a few of them groaned, but I think it'll stick. Darragh's coming over later today, I promised her a tour of Murry Hill."

'Gil, Ruto's been doing great. I know that, you know that, you know I know that. But he's taken to the training like, ah...'
`A fish to water, you could say~`
'...yeah. I suppose you're not wrong. But Darunia tells me this is the happiest he's been since they were children. To have an actual way to change things... they were destructive because that's all they could do. But now, Ruto - the both of them, actually - have somewhere to contribute their energy, and it's really showing. They both get on well with the Night Shifters, too; they've taken on brotherly sort of roles, and Ruto especially is great at calming them down if there's a disagreement. Darunia's better at talking with adults, so he's helping out at the embassy, too.'
'Honestly, how well they work together, even when doing different things? Reminds me of Roy and myself. I'm certain that we made a good choice here.'

'Oh, yeah - you remember how, way back, Roy made the excuse of looking for a park location in order to check the Gazette cornerstone without telling us about it? Well, we've been thinking back on that, and... it would be a good place for a park, really. We'll have to get approval from the city, but I doubt they'd have a problem with it. If they allow us naming rights I'm going to suggest Liberty Park, I think it fits.'

`What's up, Gildmaster Sandytuff? Sab asked me to report in for her, she's meeting with borough officials. They want it made clear that the park will still be part of Hampstead rather than us building there making it a part of the Wilds, which - she's been telling them all along that yes, she has no intention of claiming the land, her only motivation is improving the borough's welfare for everyone who lives or visits there, no catch, but I guess with all the politics it needs to drag on longer. But you'd think they'd understand her intent with, I don't know, all the help we gave to the rest of rebuilding...`

"Hey, Gil. How are you doing? I hope we didn't keep you waiting for too long. We'll be departing the city soon. I think it's all progressing well and in good hands. I finished that thing I mentioned before. I'm calling it the Blue Strider. It'll help us travel, and be a home away from home. Well... A shelter, rather. I want to think of the wilds of Arcania as a home to care for wherever, so we would never really be away from home."

"I've been talking with folks from Feytown, to make the vehicle be like their wooden ferries and not make a mess wherever we'd go. It's not the fastest, but it's just the way I wanted. You know, having caring for nature be one of your tenets definitely made me change how I think of machines. Not like I was wasteful beforehand, just neutral, I suppose. But there's great value in enforcing our creations fitting with the environment around us."

"Anyway, the Strider will house me, Sab, Ed, Irynx, and Lilly, and should have room to spare should anyone else join us. I mean, aside from Grimmy. No force can contain Grimmy. Don't worry, it's not gonna stop us from actually getting out into nature. There's a lot to see for us, but... Well, I'm not able to say how I know it. In a week or two, when we have this chat, it won't be in Murry Hill for a while. But, all of rivers and lakes are under your care, right? I'm sure we'll find a place."

'Gil, as you can probably tell - I'm talking to you from the pond I made in Liberty Park.'
`It's in the shape of your face!`
'...no, it's not. I feel like carving nature into the shape of someone's face is... somewhat weird. And even if I was going to do that - they were already worried I had ulterior motives for requesting a pond in the first place. Which... yes, having a pond here is useful for us, but my main reasoning was, well - our people and others' hydration needs, as well as a place for animals to drink from.'
`So they put it up to a vote. I'm still mad the pigeon-shaped pond didn't win.`
'It ended up, hmm... sort of a lumpy horseshoe shape, with a large tree in the center. I like it, honestly. I've put a spectrum of flowers around it, and Roy's set up some glyphs to refill it if it runs empty. The cornerstone's surrounded by flowers, too, and there's talks of turning the old Gazette building into a museum...'

** **

`Oh, heya, Gil. Uh, it's me. Sorry if you expected Sab, she's not feeling too great. I kept telling her she's overworking herself... if any of us should overwork, it's me, an hour of ritual and a bundle of incense and I'm back no problem. But it's nothing major, at least, she just needs some rest. I'd be able to tell if it were serious, and yeah, I feel a little odd, but no sense of impending doom or existential despair today---hold on, she just woke up, I'll voice for her for a few. Just like old times, huh?`

'Gil, good morning... evening... whichever time it is. Don't worry about me, I've just been feeling a bit tired. Been making sure everything's ready for the trip tomorrow. It's odd how many things living people need to travel, compared to how little I came here with... Roy says hello, by the way. He's been looking after me, hasn't left my side since I, ah, slightly collapsed. Just a little bit, I'm alright. Everyone's enforcing rest on me... I guess I can see why, but it's a little frustrating. Ah - Ed's brought me soup, I'll talk to you later.'

`So yeah. Dunno what I'm feeling from her, feels a bit different to straight-up overwork, so I'm guessing anticipation's bleeding through with it. Which, I get it. I got put on moral support duty - we'll see how long that one lasts with all the puns I've been thinking up, hah - but I'm just so hyped for whatever we'll end up finding. Really strange feeling, that, like - I entered this city as Sab's Guide, now I'm guiding countless people to your shining light. Or something like that. Iunno. We all grew so much, huh?...anyway, gonna grab me some of that soup. You won't catch me missing out on Ed's cooking if I can help it. See ya later, Gill-pickle.`

'Gil... we're about to leave, so I have to be quick. Despite everything, I still feel burdened by the past. I need a decisive, final way to lift this weight... though, maybe... Yes, I think that will work. Thanks.'

Roy leads Sabrine to the Noir, somewhere reminiscent of their first expedition there.
"So, what are you leaving?"
*'My old cloak...* Sab says. *I'm not sure I ever mentioned it, but it was originally the shroud I was wrapped in for burial. It's been a shield for me for so long, since my second chance at life... But I don't need it any more. I'm hoping it can help others in the future, if I leave it here - help them to seize the day, live without regrets, and move forwards. Like I have.'*
Roy nods. "Yeah, that sounds like it might do some good here for someone."
*'How about you?'* She asks.
Roy shakes his head. "Well... I don't think I'm as profound. I was thinking the short bow you painted when I needed one, and the overalls I've had ever since before coming to Arcania. I mended and cleaned them, before you ask."
Looking a little surprised for a second, she nods. *'Yeah... That makes sense. It's not like you need it any more...'* a couple of tears come to her eyes. *'I'm glad it helped while it could.'*

"I didn't shoot it much before making Mended Anew," Roy starts. "But it wasn't the point. It was probably the first time since coming to Arcania that I actually felt useful, like I could do something. Perhaps someone else could use that feeling too. And the overalls, well, gotta be crafty, I suppose. And they've been home to my swarm for years. I guess you can find some deeper meaning here. Deeper than all the pockets sewn onto those."
The tears fall as Sabrine listens. *'I hope so. Sounds like all these should embody supporting oneself and others... That's concepts we could always use more of.'* before she laughs slightly, *'So if I made the bow and you put it here, does the resulting being count as our child?'*
"Uh..." Roy pauses. "Maybe? Ask the Noir, I don't know how it works." Roy neatly folds the overalls and puts them on a bench, and then puts the shortbow on the same bench at the other end. "I hope that'll work."

'It should? I'm not sure how long it takes, though... I might not live to see the results. Well, so long as it helps people out, I don't mind.'
*"Same."* Roy adds. *"I suppose you wanted to say something before leaving the cloak?"*
'Yes, though... not quite about it.' She takes a deep breath, kneels and continues to speak:

'Katrine. I'm moving on, for both our sakes. I know you wouldn't want me to be tied down by the past. My reminder...'
She pulls out her revolver, newly cleaned and polished; the name **Katrine's Sorrow** gone, neatly replaced with **Katrine's Requiem**.
'I placed this on myself as a burden, to prevent me from forgetting, though it caused me many problems. With this name change, I free myself of this burden, keeping only the memory.'
The gun is returned to its holster.
'Katrine, I may not remember your real name, what you look like, or any real details - but I remember you, and I always will. If you can hear me... I love you, sis.'
As she finishes speaking, she gently releases the shroud, letting it float where it will as the Noir takes it, eyes sparkling with both tears and the determination to move forwards.
Roy puts his hand on Sabrine's shoulder. *"Perhaps we'll meet whoever the cloak gives life to. Or we won't. We'll see. Anyway, shall we head back to the Strider? I suppose it's time to go."*
Sabrine nods and stands back up, taking his hand. 'It is, or so Kukudh says. Let's go.'
As they head back, her walk is somewhat wobbly, both from emotion and tiredness, but there's clearly a burden lifted from her mind and heart.

Lucy beams with excitement... 

Another Bo has seen before is about to ride, Lucy tells him. A bright flash of light herolds the way... But... Something is off...

 Something, Bo hasnt quite fully expected. He is joined by two souls this time..."uh... This is new...." Another light beams from above..."t-three? All at once?!?!" As the light fades, the three souls sit formless in front of him, much like wisps.

Bo sits, blinking curiously. "Um... Uh... Hiya you three... " bo smiles warmly as he haphazardly waves, still confused. "Now then... Lets see your story shall we?" He asks as he bows graciously. As lucy flies around... She tilts her head as, something off-sets her. 

Before bo could start his normal ritual of playing his mother's lullaby... A song begins to echo from 2 of the 3 wisps. Lucy quickly moves in, and boops one of the wisps. Bo looks on, confused as the wisp takes form, and his ears twitch to the melody the goblin before him is singing. As Lucy boops the next wisp, the remaining 2 wisps take form. A Goblin in armor, and a small puppy... The song becomes shockingky clear to Bo now. The two goblins before him... Are singing his mother's lullaby. He quickly adds to the melody andnsings along, much to the suprise of Rockman and Leaf. It takes a moment for bo to recognize one of the goblins, before he begins to be licked by a small puppy. It is indeed a very small dog, but his bark echoes through the realm Bo travels in.

Bo pets the puppy only briefly, before a memory flashes in his head, the oasis. "HEY! ..... Ain't you... Gil's friend?" Bo asks. The male goblin gives bo a thumbs up and smiles.
"Yeap! You were there in Gil's oasis the day he appeared, weren't ya?" Lucy beams in, and in an instant, he witnesses the life story of the 3... Of Rockman, Leaf, and Rush. 

Bo's eyes grow wide with excitement as he see's Sandigil, the coins passed around for his mayoral candidacy. He's excited to watch....up until bo himself see's the horrors in town square, Sandigil's head on a pike. The fight with the Hunger... And the wish rockman had made... To wish Sandigil back to life. He quickly moves over and shakes Rickman's hand, as Leaf steps forward and asks how it was that Bo knew their song. 

Dormant memories flood Bo's mind, of being a smol bun. He had scrapped his knee... And his mother begain singing. 
"Mama, where'd you learn that song?" Bo asked.
All she responded with, was a smile as he kept singing.

"My mother sang it to me... Later on she finally told me, that lullaby had been passed down for generations." Bo chuckkes. Rockman and Leaf both look towards each other and smile, holding hands.

Meanwhile, the puppy Rush flies around chasing a panicking Lucy. Voices echo from the two as they spin around in the air.
"play? Play? Play?" -rush
"Aaaaaah he's so slobery!" -lucy

Bo, Rockman, and Leaf all laugh together as the carpet, at first unknowingly to Bo, slowly rises up. Higher and higher as a light beams down from the sky above.

As they sit and talk, Bo eventually notices the change in scenery. As golden light fills the area, a small fish flies down, spinning around Leaf. Leaf's face beams with joy as Rush and Lucy fly over. The trio ascend up even higher as Rockman and Leaf begins to phase back into living boddies. Bo looks on in amazement as the puppy grows and his bark begins to deepen.

On the banks near by, a form fades as they smile up to the sky. Web sighs as their voice echoes.

**Eliot:** 
After spending a bit further time with Jigsaw, Raxacoricofallapatorius, and Mike, Eloise excuses herself to return to the Crepes and Crits Café, meeting with Willow outside to have another heavy conversation along with collecting some personal belongings,  Before returning to Cael'fii and Demetrius.

Eloise takes a few hours each day to begin teaching Sabrine Arcanian Sign Language, (at no cost) which Roy and Kukudh are welcome to participate in. She aids in rebuilding the park in New Hempstead using a few uses of Plant Growth. 

As everything settles down and Eloise has more time to sort out her thoughts and feelings she asks those closest to her to refer to them as El, and while they still didn't quite feel like themselves they felt better than before.

El says goodbye to the part of themselves that was Eloise one week after their death and rebirth. They are glad to have had the opportunity to form the happy memories they did and  come to peace with who they were once upon a time, but it is not who they are.

After informing Demetrius of where El was at, in regards to finding themselves, El begins to grow more secretive and recluse. Not out of any wrongdoing or deteriorating mental state, simply the impending deadline of the pact made. The deadline and responsibility weigh on El as if they were carrying the whole cafe and the foundation of which it stood upon their back. 

On September 6th, 1776 two days prior to the deadline El presents a masterful blend of tea to Demetrius, beaming with pride, glad to finally have kept their part of their deal. However, it was still lacking something and it was not enough to leave Demetrius speechless nor was it the perfect blend. Shattered, heartbroken and defeated, realizing that no matter how much effort they put in within the next two days it would not be enough. The months they had spent afraid of the outside finally taking its toll. Through tears El pledged their eternal service to Demetrius until they were able to get it right.

Shortly following this pledge, El put Willow in charge of the cafe until the debt was paid off. They donned their tailcoat and accompanied Demetrius most places, when allowed, and offered their services where applicable as a butler. Secretly El was happy to spend as much time as they could in Demetrius' company, and it was a secret not well hidden from the other court members of Feyrytown. But El kept their demeanor professional regardless of who Demetrius was meeting with and always had tea on hand. On the extraordinarily rare occurrence where meetings took a darker turn, El also performed the duties of a bodyguard. Not that the ancient fey needed the help, but as a way to help insure neither resorted to their violent pasts. 
Six months after their death, El returns to being Eliot, once more comfortable in who he is. Eliot dyes his hair back to his well known mint color, but there is a single streak of gold along the left side. Three years of companionship and servitude to Demetrius pass before they are granted passage, for a singular day, to where Demetrius' home once was. Upon seeing the beauty, Eliot understood what his tea had been missing. He separates himself from Demetrius for a short time to gather some flowers and a bit of the soil. Saving them for a later surprise.

On the anniversary of their fifth year together Eliot invites Demitrius on a surprise trip for their anniversary, Eliot is shy but proud to show Demetrius the Demiplane he had crafted for the couple to share, a replica of Demetrius’ home. It wasn’t quite perfect, but it was enough for the two of them to call their own home.

content:
Years pass, and Eliot grows older yet Demitrius remains the same. Eliot has a longing to be part of Demitrius’ life for as long as the fey had already lived. But knows he can’t, instead he looks into something originally only a fleeting desire from his youth, and came back to him briefly in the presence of a certain radiant familiar. Eliot looks into dragons and their kin. A child the couple could raise together, and not be bound by Eliot’s own mortality. He didn’t want Demetris to grieve his passing, or worsen it by a child of theirs also passing long before the archfey’s time was up.

It took several more years before Eliot was able to get an egg with help from Prosser stopping some smugglers. Then presenting it to Demetrius, a large egg coated in deep red scales. Despite the off color Eliot consider’s Trapero as a name for the dragon, but discusses it with Prosser first. They mention that if it were to be named in Trapero’s honor they’d prefer it to be Prospero, the name the twins held before they were split.  

Soon after receiving the egg the small red dragon is running amok and driving Eliot up walls just to keep up with the wild child and its flames. Despite all the stress a smile never leaves his face, particularly when seeing young Prospero and Demetrius bonding while Eliot cleans scorch marks and regrows flowers.

Many uneventful years pass, and Eliot enjoys the chaotic peace with his small family. But he knows his life is drawing near. Many other humans he’s known of his years have passed, and he’s seen waves upon wave’s of Sutri’s own children become adults in their own right, and even see some of them move on to whatever happened next. He takes Demetrius out one one more date, to the small little cafe that began it all, and brews up a pot of tea for them both. A special recipe he had figured out oh so many years ago, on the trip to Demitrius’ home. A recipe he didn’t need to be confident in, a recipe he knew was the one. He sat across from Demitrius and acted as if there was nothing special about the tea by taking the first sip, before relishing the look on his partner’s face and making a gentle comment that he finally paid of his debt for fulfilling his childhood dream, and being thankful to have helped make so many other people’s dreams come true, including his own, all at the side of the most wonderful partner.

The Speaker bids farewell to all of his friends at the city and embarks on his first trip out of Arcania borders. He journeys south for Meorys’s hometown to drop her off there. Meorys tells the Speaker that they both came from here and that the Speaker was once a noble of this lands, the Faranells she said. The Speaker has no memories of this whatsoever but one this is for sure, the person that left this place for Empire city is no longer. That person died long ago and now the Speaker, a brand new person, stands in their place. Meorys and the Speaker bid each other farewell, marking the end to the Ball Eater crew.

    The Speaker embarks on his next adventure. Time to finish up his deal with a dragon. He lays out his tarot deck in front of him, the world card face up serving to strengthen his connection to the spirit world as he calls out for Nidhogg. Invoking the name of Nidhogg with the intention to speak with him gives the Speaker the feeling of his cold breath wrapping around your skin. A low growl rumbles against his chest, the dragon of Yggdrasil is listening.

The Speaker takes a deep breath to collect his thoughts. "The war against Britain is over, Arcania has won. Though I assume you already know this. I am here to hold up my end of the bargain. I am awaiting your orders." The Speaker speaks with forced politeness. "Cross you the eastern Ocean. Bring yourself to bear against my enemies, Ephemeral." The Speaker grins mentally. "Nice timing, I was about to go there myself." He then scolds himself as he regains seriousness. "Enemies? Odin?"

"The Aesir move against the once and future king. My people enslaved by the Hanging one, the one eyed God of Thieves and Heroes is bringing the berzerker rage against the Knights of the Round. The war is pitched and laying waste to all of the lands between them. Gods who call themselves good ignore the Gods who call themselves evil to make war against one another. And in the midst of these battles, Arthur's Dragon Merlin moves against my people. My servants among the living."

"And this is where I step in." The Speaker lets out a breath of relief. He was bracing himself for Nidhogg ordering him to do unspeakable atrocities, continuing the fight against Britain is no such thing. "Who am I fighting with? Is there a representative of your people I am to meet up with?"

"Saint George the Dragon Slayer is named among the great heroes of Britannia. Morgana Le fey would see Merlin destroyed. Aid her in this and then she shall aid you in the defeat of Saint George. Without his dragon lance, my people: the trolls, the dark elves, the giants shall no longer fear that Jörmungandr be slain."

The Speaker nods. "I understand. I will head out for Britain, seek out these people, and defeat the king's dragon. I shall do this to uphold our agreement and to help your people. Evil, good, or anything else I shall not let anyone be oppressed by the British no longer. I'll be meeting you once more after this is all over, in one way or another."

"You will not meet me again. You are my unshackling. You have bound yourself to my service. And that service extends into your death. At the time of your death, I will finally abdicate Hel and name you my successor. Foolish mortal. Your death will be an unending task of tending to the unwanted dead."

The Speaker flinches and nearly falls to the ground. This is the catch he's been expecting, but in all his wildest imaginations, this wasn't in them. He is speechless.

Nidhogg fades. His command is complete.

He remembers all he's been through to put him in this situation and regains his composure. He starts speaking to no one in particular. "As Speaker for the Dead, I accept this." Not like he had a choice. "Unwanted the souls under me may be, but voiceless they will not. I shall serve as a warning for those who unnecessarily give away parts of themselves. Those who purposely throw away themselves shall end up under the watch of the Nameless Speaker." 

With a heavy heart, the speaker sails for Britain.

    Without Morgana’s long accrued knowledge of Merlin and its weaknesses, the Speaker wouldn’t be able to take out the dragon and without the Speaker and his crew Morgana would’ve lacked the needed firepower and resilience to outmatch Merlin. It is only through their cooperation that Merin would fall. Through the help of the spirits and the brute strength of the nordic dead, Merlin is flushed out of his lair. Morgana’s magicks keep him distracted and bogged down while the artillery fire of the Raven Queen tears away at his defenses. Taking a page out of Captain Midask’s book on how to slay a dragon the Speaker constructs a volatile creation using the leftovers of Meorys’s pigments, tempered with the expertise of the mechanic onboard. With this ramshackle contraption of oil flasks and ball bearings, Merlin is laid to rest. The wings of Arthur fall and the forces of Odin descend upon the British isles. The speaker’s job isn’t over yet however, there is still one foe that stands between him and his duty. Saint George the Dragonslayer needs to be cast down.

content:
The fight with Merlin renders the Raven Queen grounded and its crew busy. The Speaker and Morgana alone face the saint. This battle plays out differently from the clash with Merlin. Without his ship around them, the Speaker and Morgana are vulnerable and Saint George proves to be a highly competent combatant. It is only through sheer luck and with the strength of spirits, quite literally, that the Speaker continues to fight. With berserkers surrounding him and Morgana’s magic manipulating the tides of the battle, Saint George is almost beaten, but his aim proves true and his dragonlance punches through dragon-like flesh as it skewers the Speaker. The Speaker doesn’t go without a fight however as a well time point blank shatter spell manages to break apart the lance of Saint George and renders him open towards Morgana’s attacks.

    Thus this is the end to the Speaker’s tale. A sorceress beside him, promising to take care of the airship and crew he leaves behind and finally giving it the proper chance to be more than just a vessel for war, a large hole in his chest letting out blood at an alarming rate, and no raven, fey, mad scientist, or mender in site to bring his spirit back. The Speaker’s eyes go dull and lifeless and his spirit goes straight down.

The inseparable pair of mice continued their work at the café before accepting the offer to be Awakened on April 22, 1779.

However, they did not stay at the café for long after their Awakening. Armed with their wits, their acts, and each other the pair made their way to Broadway. 

The pair did their best as actors among the scene but for all their heart and skill they were often typecast or used solely in narration roles due to their small stature. 

Undeterred from their struggles the pair worked more diligently and became playwrights and directors instead. And while their small size made it difficult for them as performers it became an unlikely asset in their new directions allowing them to give better presentations of what they are looking for during rehearsals and casting. And on more than one occasion dashing across stage to provide an understudy their lines should the actor freeze up during a performance.

As actors they were constantly told they had the gift, but as writers and directors they were able bring their dreams and acts succefully to the stage.

No one is quite sure what happened to the pair however. One day they simply vanished. However, on a rare occasion a new script is delivered, without any author or credentials, and yet these mysterious plays are often great successes for the directors bold enough to try and bring these plays to life.

Matteo and Despo's Bibliography includes:
A nine part series of plays of warrior monks far off in the Astral Sea, a harrowing tale of romance, betrayal, the strength of ones will, and a mysterious Force that flows through all things.

A three act play telling the tale of an cursed piece of jewelry and a group of heroes questing to destroy it, having many hardships and separations along the way.

A series of plays about a local legend, some titanic dinosaur that both causes destruction to the city, but also protects it from other titans.

A play about a minstrel that lives in the sewers that strikes ever couple decades, and a group of misfits that ends its terror.

And many many more.

Mictlan

Mictlan does not leave right away. They spend several more weeks in town, helping with the rebuilding efforts as best they can. Drop by the library a few times, scribbling fiercely as if their life depends on it. The time is used getting better at being in their own skin, settling in somewhere in the midst of their feathers and learning the art of a smile. 

At the end of the three weeks, they know they do not belong anymore. Mictlan could, if they really tried, but wanderlust has come with the snow-white feathers and they… they want to see. There are only so many years left in their life, after all, and so many places left in the world. 

Before they leave, Mictlan drops by Ferrytown. They greet the shifter children, smiling in only the way only they know how. Enter the herb shop, singing something high and melodious to the plants in Celestial with an underpinning of something deeper in the throat. It somehow still works.

They leave as suddenly as they entered, with a silver for the ferry and the plants glistening, watered. 

Eρευνα stands empty in the docks, waiting for its next owner. There’s a book hidden under a floorboard in there, words spaced between arcane sigils in a sort of a journal most cannot read. 

The shifter speaks with any they come across as they exit the city, because politeness dictates it. They are happy, but brief, and will not be stayed. 

A feathered silhouette passes through the land, carrying a bag and following the land due north-northeast. Their steps are light along the road, a familiar shape hovering behind Mictlan’s shoulder all eyes and feathers and rings. Just before they leave sight of the city they step forward and *changes* into something with a large wingspan, striking out with joyous beats of their wings. Their cousin-familiar (Aefirael) follows, spinning. 
** **

That’s not the last place they are spotted, but their movements become erratic over the years. Mictlan seems to go for knowledge and history, both in the past and that which will become it. They seem to seek out flight, but not too much after the first few years. 

(They do not make a deal with the fae, but do consider it the first couple of years. No, they decide later; The sky is missed, but even before they did not spend all day in the air.)

Mictlan never stays in once place for long. They do not quite revisit places, either, as far as can be told. Throughout the years they get better at magic as one must if they keep on that path, and perhaps they meet people they saw earlier in life. Find ways of extending their own life, as they suppose most mortals must go for once they see so much more that they can do. The celestial- or, well, not celestial anymore, not for a long time- writes it down in a growing spellbook and moves on.

They may only stay for the duration of their natural lifetime, but that had ended twice already before they even left the city. And yet, there is an acute sense of mortality. Attachments trail behind them like a path of stardust, some growing stronger and others tapering out. Age catches up to the best, unless it doesn’t.

Perhaps it takes only decades. Perhaps it takes lifetimes. But a feathered serpent loops around whatever the old city has become as they leave again for sights unseen and unknown. Once. Twice. Thrice, waving a scaled wing as it flies into the rising sun. Their cousin is not with them. 

It's taken them so many years, so many lifetimes, but at last they know where they’re going. 

Where they’ve always been going. 

Home. The long way round.
There we go!

__**LEAVING**__
"Do you still remember the times before we met each other?" Irynx asks the other people on the Strider.

Sabrine laughs. 'I mean… you're asking me, there wasn't exactly that much time. But yes, the times before, of fear and mistrust… I have to actively think to remember those now.'

Orphy sighs, adjusting the seat belts on a sleepy Corbianne. `Ah. The good old days, when our lives were constantly in danger! Wait, no. Empire City was worse, actually.`

Ed chuckles and mutters "What's life without a little danger?"

"Back in my home town it wasn't that bad," Roy says from the driver's seat, fiddling with some controls before they depart. "And arrival to the City was pretty bland and boring. Overall improvement from that, I suppose."

`I remember absolutely nothing!` Kukudh chimes in, sounding happier than they should about this. Sabrine looks to Roy, 'I'd still like to visit your hometown some time, if possible. Though I understand if you wouldn't want to.'

"Honestly…" Roy thinks for a moment. "I don't think going back to the old lands is a good idea anymore. My swarm did kinda send me here so I'm out of the way, and well, I haven't really fulfilled the task given to me. For one, I'm not expanding the swarm's influence, and then on top of that I kind of have my own separate swarm from my town's one. Which they should've expected, but not much of that plan was really planned."

Sabrine nods. 'Understandable.' `Hey, could always send me just to look around.` '…no, with that, I think best not. Same reasoning as, ah… earlier's moving on discussion.'

"Swarm," Cor murmurs, before Orphy soothes her back into a sleepy state.

"Alright, everyone seated or planted, and Grimmy ready to follow?" Roy says, doing a quick headcount over the seats behind him. "Let's roll, then. The west awaits."

__**WILLIAM**__
Orphy starts to fly around the strange tabaxi in a circle. Irynx is busy braiding flowers into her daughter's hair, but looks up to eye her familiar. "What are you doing? You're not a vulture."

`Shhh. I was just observing him.` Orphy lands on a branch in front of the tabaxi, beak uncomfortably close to his face. `So, William, right? You… have really great vibes. And also, no bad angles. Except maybe from below.` He swings to hang upside down on the branch. `Your chin looks a little wider and the lighting makes your—`

"Hey, stop being weird." Irynx scolds him.

"Stop being weird, Toffee!" Cor repeats.

`Someone say vibe?` Kukudh starts flicking the tabaxi's ears. `Haha, catto go brrr.` A glance from Sabrine; they stick their tongue out, turn into spider-crab form, and just chill on William's shoulder.

Will is unmoved by the familiar's shenanigans. He is calm in this chaos. Even with a dinosaur looking to put him in her mouth. 

Sabrine sighs. 'Apologies for Kukudh's… antics. They're somewhat restless.'

"Yep." Roy nods. "Standard Kukudh behavior. Don't worry, we know who's taking the next turn cleaning the Strider."

Without looking back up, Irynx adds, "Orphy will join them, too. Because I say so."

"Then I will join them as well!" Cheerfully says Will, and Ed just facepalms.

`Man, he's such a great person too!` Orphy squawks in exasperation.

"I just want to stay close to Ed, so I will do anything in my power to help their friends. That's not really being a great person. It's just being decent and considerate of others."

"Well, if you volunteer, welcome on board." Roy says, already having in mind how to split the job so Kukudh gets the worst part.

__**GOODBYE GRIMLOCK**__
Sabrine reaches out to scritch Grimmy behind the ears, casting Speak with Animals as she does so. 'Say hello to everyone for us, alright?'

Grimlock nods as she gets scritches under her chin. ||I can't take care of you anymore, my pets. Now you must go off on your own. But the people in Empire still need me.||

Roy joins in with Speak With Animals. "With you looking over the city, I'm sure we won't have anything to worry about."

Sabrine and Kukudh start to take on translator duty for those without animal-speaking capability.

"Thank you for being with us, Grim." Irynx places a palm over the side of Grimlock's head.

Ed is a snotty mess hearing about this, and is clinging to Grimmy's leg. Lilly also creeps up on Grimlock's other leg before returning to her flower pot. "I will come back to visit you then… I promise." They let go and look up at their huge friend. 

||I will come visit you first.|| Grimlock gives Ed one last lick, before lumbering off eastward. She looks back to the group one last time and roars loud and mighty, before continuing on her way secure in the knowledge that she will return.

__**BIRTHDAY**__
It was in Ed's worst interest to tell everyone of their birthday two days on the road from their last stop. Now they won't be able to get anything *fun* for a celebration. They'll probably only have barrels of water and two snarky familiars because of this mistake. Oh, and of course, William.

`Should've told us sooner. Well, guess we'll have to make do~` Kukudh swipes some leaves and sprinkles them over the birthday fluff.

"Well, we can make something out of what we got. It calls for a celebration. So, uh… I'll make goodberry pie? Won't be as good as what you make, but we'll try our best."

`Hey, hey,` Orphy adds. `we can't let the birthday bunny know what we plan to do now, can we? Between all of us… well, Ed got all the talent for food, so I can't help in here. I'm on Team Keep Ed out of the Kitchen. Come on, let's go let's go!` He flies out of the kitchen.

The Shadow of the Umbral Cup

    I had a long road ahead of me once the war was over. I was a mender; I was fighting in the war to rebuild what this city was meant to be about. In my first life I was building for the greatness of working men and women, we gave blood, sweat, and tears to get the roads laid out and the buildings stacked to the clouds. I died for that dream; my work was bastardized by business men hiring necromancers to keep the taskforce moving. At first, I was just another mindless builder. I saw the abuse the living workers were put through, almost like the top-hats wanted people to die just to make easier to manage workers. That’s what made me snap awake again. I came back full of rage; I beat back the taskmasters that would whip and try to break us. Andross Mortem may have been dead, but there was someone else standing in his Body, something else inside his Bones. That’s where you all met me.

----- scene 1 a walk down sesame sweet

“Good to see you come by Bones, so many have left for all over Arcania. How have things been in Kingsbridge?” It was always good to stop by Sesame Sweet to see Fuddles. Sonny has been doing a lot of planning and packing lately so I could only assume they were going to leave too. Thought it’s best to enjoy company while I have it, along with these shamrock cupcakes. 
“Things have been bustling. People got attracted to the new name on the umbral cup, but maybe I need to get a painter to put Gil on the front of it. They want to know who sandy is, givin me all kinds of funny looks.” I do my best to give her a smile, but I’m not the best at hiding what’s on my mind.
“Something wrong?” 
“I’ve just…thought a lot about Gil. And these headstones we all placed. The one in hampstead is part of what caused this mess, so somebody has to stick around and watch over them.” I could tell she understood, but looking to the room where sonny was working on maps for his next goal meant she knew she had a different road ahead. She got up to go talk with him while I habitually took out my matchless pipe. Good thing they invested in outdoor seating or else she’d have given me hell for smoking out the business. They finally came out after a couple minutes. Sonny looking spry as ever. “Howdy Sonny, heard you were planning quite a trip.” He wore a nice suit, changed to a traditional green for the vest, matched his skin now. His body may be a frog now but the green blood in his veins will never go away.

----- scene 2 back-alley bargain

“Yeah, but I always have time for my friends old man, the Mrs. tells me you were going to plant roots here in empire. We’re planning on living here. It’s just, there’s a lot out in different places that we can’t forget about. Anything we can do to help?” I Thought he’d never ask. 
“I’m looking after something important for Gil. I’ve made a good hiding spot for it and promised to keep it a secret, but to make sure it stays protected I had to find something solid, timeless.”
“Well, we got all kinds of magic in this town. Maybe before we leave, we can go through the library, or see if some of the cartels have something to help.”
“How about a bit of both?”
“Well, one thing at a time. Sis was always into magic and history, found a little bit of a tip involving a thingy. Thingies are usually pretty useful to start.”

There were a lot more guns than I expected. I knew Sonny was in cahoots with a lot of underhanded smugglers but I didn’t realize he heard a rumor about a local mafia like this. Some group invested in Ferrytown and Hampstead that had the leftovers of the lycanthrope torture supply from the gazette, among other magical goods like the ‘thing’ he mentioned. Why didn’t I follow Sonny behind those crates? This trolley doesn’t hold up against bullet fire. If that volt thrower guy got too close, I’d have nowhere to go. “I thought it too Bones, but in slang ‘it smells like a troll’ is code for not respecting someone and sending hitmen later!” That’s a lot of gunfire, oh boy. “You didn’t know.” Took me a moment to think, did sonny get shot or did he shoot someone? I had to move. The staff and twig were still saving my ass at least. Just gotta be faster than them. One hand using the staff, and one to outdo their mage stopper.
“I’ll keep that in mind!” That’s the volt thrower down, now where is- Ah, there she is. Damn that woman can pull weight, those are orcs. are they breathing? Well, they ain’t getting up that’s for sure.
“I got the, thing, sonny what did you say this was?”
“Ancient cryptid stone thingy, I don’t know it just sounded magic!”
“If we got it let’s get out of here you two. They ain’t slowing down.” There was no time for picks, this lock is breaking. The two horses would work for us. They really are a cute couple. A shame there wasn’t a sunset for him to ride her off to.
“We’ll uh, we’ll lead them this way don’t worry the library should help you.”
“Thanks, I owe you Both one, put it on my tab will ya?”

“These guys aren’t half as bad as swarms of redcoats. I could take this in my sleep” Fuddles sure could, I would hate to be on her bad side any day. Not as long as she has that axe, no, even without the axe she’s a force of nature.
“I just hope you’re still here when we come back, don’t go dying on us again!”
“Not planning on it!” Well, only one way to find out if this can help. One trip to the library, hopefully this can be a one book stop otherwise this could get dicey. At least those punks won’t follow me in there, I’d rather face redcoats than what they do to people causing a ruckus. This thing is pretty heavy so hopefully it’s useful.

----- scene 3 an avalanche of knowledge

Actually a little noisy in the library. Lots of footsteps trying to learn more about so much that happened near the end of the war. Months of research in here was rough but this is definitely getting somewhere. ‘Cryptids are attracted to historical events, a divination ability they have to just know when something memorable is going on. When you hear word of cryptids be aware of everything around you no matter how mundane or insignificant it appears.’ That explained a couple of things. Still nothing about this thing Sonny acquired for me. ‘Cryptids are also known to be attracted to places and objects that have survived for long periods of time. They can sometimes be found protecting ancient sites or treasures that have been used in historical events. Bringing such items into solitary places might attract cryptids, it is suggested that when transporting these objects to travel in large groups and move quickly.’ I went to the desk to see if the librarian on shift knows anything about this. Given the no talking policy I’ll just use a telepathy spell. “Hey, you wouldn’t happen to be studied on mystic items relating to cryptids would you?” he gave me a look and a deep psychic chuckle at the question.

“hahhahhah, yes. I know all kinds of things about cryptids and magical items. But that’s a lot of very sensitive knowledge. But I’m glad you’ve been thoroughly digging into BOOOOOOKS!” He sure was a colorful fella. He had a bounce to him, like a child’s ball. But he seems the type to know his stuff, only those types have the confidence to wear a fez like that. “I’d suggest that you be sure to respect them as part of the ancient magic of Arcania. Not all are reasonable.” 
“I reckon they wouldn’t be. I’m trying to find ways to protect something indefinitely. I got a bit of a passion project going on.”
“Passion, joy, excitement! That’s what we live for! When you find purpose it’s always good to make a plan and give it everything you got! It puts a smile on my face to see a friend of Gil’s trying to build on his legacy, it was always so sad before when he was a hero in death.”
“You knew sandy? How?”
“That’s a story for another day, and perhaps if you read enough BOOKS! You’ll come across the tale much like that vampire novel you’ve been reading. How is it by the way?”
“Ah, it’s a tense read. They’re about to sit down with Strahd and discuss the release of their friend. It’s also at the same time as the previous chapter where they had a jailbreak for the kid, so the big man isn’t going to be too happy. And that’s not a good place to have a ruckus.”
“I see, these are the kind of stories any brave soul is able to venture through. Who knows maybe you’ll be able to live forever, in a BOOOOK!”<:ArchivistDaysong:862360291119071232>

The new congress offices were a maze to get through. There was only one person I knew I would be able to get in touch with for a hand. “I can’t help you Mr. mortem. Now we have time, me and Washington have an understanding that we have a lot of work to set a strong foundation for this country. You understand right?” It was a surprise. He had always been so excited to head on an adventure. 
“Well, I guess I should have expected you to have these priorities in this office. Ah, that’s not meant to be an insult. I appreciate you’re working on the system to be better than how it was written at congress. Good to see we stand a little closer than we thought even if I still get concerned about some things.”
“I still think you worry too much, it’s safer this way. We can’t let tyranny be easily accessible and this is the best way to do it. It would take three tyrants to manipulate the system and that will only get more difficult after me and good old Washington ratify more definitions to the positions”
“And, what about this cryptid hunt?” Finn seems deep in thought, like he’s debating on telling me, but he obviously knows.

“Nolan uh…Nolan found something about that. He and Viv were tracking the mafia’s movements and found them heading out into the noir. Somethings out there, and but they don’t seem to have found what they were looking for.”
“Same one sonny brought me to?” Finn gives a nod. “So, they were going to take this to the noir. They must have planned to use it as bait to attract something out there, at least that’s what the library was telling me.”
“Andross, I really don’t think you should be looking for trouble like this. It’s not like you, you’re a hardworking man your skills and the knowledge you have could be better used helping us build something new.”
“Finn, Andross is dead. He’s not coming back even if I’m the spitting image of him. There’s just nothing that can change that.” I turned to leave but I could feel a tug on my arm before I was able to leave the door.
“You say you’re doing this for the mender, are you sure he’s somebody you want to be following? I don’t mean to sound rude but are you sure you shouldn’t just let his work go? He did enough.” I had to sigh and shake my head.
“There’s always more. Just like how the redcoats almost tore this whole city down, somebody else will come along and try to ruin all of it. I’m making sure what Gil built, what we’ve all built, doesn’t crumble. You do that here, making your policies. I have my own way of it.” I know he understood, he meant well with what he said but I can’t just up and tell him what I’m doing.

“Well about time you came around. “might…be weeks.”

I could only give them a nod as we prepared. Got a lot of grub and scrolls for the road. Who knows what hell we’re in for. Managed to catch Irynx at the grove. I…needed to ask the egg something.

You stick to going out only in the fog, at first, staying in an abandoned building any other time. It's easy enough to hide there, and the pigeons are at least good companionship. But then the borough burns, and the fog fades, and reconstruction begins. You start to venture out during the night, to find something, anything, you can use as food - not that you need to eat, but chewing things helps you stay sane - but often, you come back to whatever shelter in the rubble you've managed to piece together to find it cleared away, and multiple times you've been disturbed from your rest - not sleep, never sleep - by people approaching, and have had to scramble to find a new place before anyone finds you.

Until one day, it all changes. You come back from a remarkably successful hunting expedition with a couple of lilac, juicy berries, to find - again - that your temporary shelter is mid-deconstruction. A quick look, and no one seems to be around besides a few pigeons; you allow yourself the luxury of a curse.
`Language!`
You look around, startled and fearful - but no one's there. You hear a slight giggling, though, and follow the sound to... one of the pigeons? Apparently mistaking your look of confusion for one of condemnation, the... pigeon? continues, `Yeah, yeah, I know I'm a hypocrite for that. Sorry, sorry.`
That's it. You've clearly lost what sanity remained. On a closer look, the pigeon has four wings - two of which are like a beetle's, three legs, horns... You pinch yourself, it hurts. So it's certainly not a dream, at least... though that means no chance of waking up from it. The pigeon is speaking again.
`So, uh, I guess you were sleeping here or something? Sorry about that, but you know we've got actual shelters set up, right?`
You didn't - but it's not like they'd accept you, anyway. So to save face, you mumble something about allergies. `Oh, we got some in the park without iron or silver if you need that. Or if it's a people allergy, we can find you some place to set up safely.`
This pigeon doesn't quit, do they...? They're peering at you closely, as if with recognition, before their eyes go wide. So this is where it ends.

`Hey, sorry if this is offensive at all. But, uh, you do know you're dead, right?`
...their question throws you off a bit, why would they apologise? Regardless, it won't change the outcome; you nod, and hold up the berries. 'Before you kill me, please... let me have one last meal, such as it were.'
`Oh, hey, that's where those berries I dropped got to.` ...they dropped these? `I'd ask why you think I'd kill you, but, uh... Been through that already. Trust me, I know. Well, second-hand---first-hand---one-and-a-half-hand? Dunno how it counts for me. My situation's a little complex.`
You stare in confusion as they shrug with both pairs of wings. `Long story. Just know you're not the first one I've Guided through this. Alright, so, from the sounds of it you've got no support at present, right? I'd get Sab to come talk to you, but she's officiating a wedding - who has weddings at dawn, anyway? And that's coming from someone who's awake then. But yeah. You got a few options...`
The pigeon starts rambling. A lot of the names they're spouting sound vaguely familiar, but you can't think where from... Their words seem to boil down to there being three places you can take shelter right now - the shelters in Hampstead or in 'Murry Hill', wherever that is, or... your ears prick up, did they just mention 'people like you'?

They seem to have picked up on your renewed interest. `Yeah, thought so. You're not the first Reborn they've taken in, and you won't be the last, either.  Alright, so - for the security of everyone who lives there, I can't take you straight to the Underfolk, but---`
'They're real? I thought they were just a legend, or a boogeyman to scare the children.'
`And that belief is exactly why we can't tell people where they live without a meeting. Thank you for coming to my birb talk.`
Though the pigeon's voice is serious, it also sounds kind - you get the feeling they're not scolding you, just stating a fact.
`So let's see. Most likely people to be able to set up a meeting at this hour are, hmm. You know where the cemetery is, and Murry Hill Park?` You know the first, but not the second, and tell the pigeon such. `Works out - I gotta get back to the park for a delivery, but I can delay a little bit to lead you there if needed, or you can just head to the cemetery.`
`If you wanna talk to someone as quick as possible, head to the cemetery, ask for Secel - she's the cute tiefling who took over recently - tell her Kukudh sent ya, and give her this note.` They pull some paper from their feathers, which has a scrawled, barely legible message - all you can make out is what looks like Infernal, and the signature `♡ Kukudh`.
`Alternative option - you can wait for Sab to be done with the wedding, I'll lead you back to the park. It'll take longer, but Sab's been in your situation before - I'm her Guide, that's how I know so much - so if you'd rather talk about it more first, there's your option.`

You think for a moment, and make your decision; the pigeon nods. `Got it. Don't you worry about a thing. And blessings of Sandigill on you or however Sab says it.`
Later that day, you're meeting with a representative of the Underfolk, and soon after, they've set you up with a shelter, with knowledge of how to adapt to your new life... with a family.
And weeks later, you run into the pigeon again, perching on the shoulder of a short Grung woman -  she smiles at you, a knowing smile, and the pigeon bows dramatically, saying just a few words as the two pass; `Seize the day, and stay determined, friend~`

Great. You're still stuck. Marv and Roman kept saying "don't worry, boss, we've got it, we can fix the car", but it's been half a day already. You got maybe two hours to the nearest town, and you'll get there before dusk only if you move soon. Which doesn't look likely. You shake your head and start thinking about making a camp for the night, and which of your employees are gonna be on watch. 

Frustrating.

Then a voice calls out to you from along the road.
"Hello there! Blessings of Sandigill to you. You seem to be having a bit of a trouble."

You look up. It's a man in a long coat, with long hair, and a wooden branching staff. Either a druid, or a weirdo. Or, possibly, a weird druid. Beside him, a short grung woman.
"Good evening" you reply. "Our engine's busted. We'll have to camp somewhere nearby."
"The town's not that far away. Let me have a look at that engine, you'll be back on the road in no time." the urban druid, for the lack of a better term, replies.
You can't help but raise an eyebrow. "Are you sure you know your way around engines?"
The man laughs heartily. "You're stuck anyway, what's the harm in trying?"

Before you can reply, he walks over to Marv and Roman, still bickering, and starts talking with them. You go a bit away for a quick smoke. They seem to be nodding to him, and let him to the engine. He does something weird with his staff and a wrench pops out of it. He gets to the engine.

You can see him doing some weird magic, and some... insects? Yeah, insects, coming out of his sleeves, forming into a hand, and moving into the engine. He waits a moment, talking with the woman in the meantime, and hits the engine with the wrench once. A bit of black liquid pours out, and into a bucket he quickly moved into place. He seems to be casting some other spell on it afterwards, and after a few quick taps, the engine whirrs back into life. Marv and Roman are nodding to one another, and you almost dropped the cigarette from your mouth.

"There you go, friend." the... druid? says. "Too much tension on on the transmission and it snaps. You should be good for two or three towns over, but the first parts shop you come across, get a replacement. Not much more I can do without access to parts out here."
"T-thanks. You really saved our skin." you muster.
"Don't mention it. Good luck to you on your way."
"Do you maybe need a ride there?" you ask.
"It's fine. We got all we need, and the night's still young. Great time for wandering."
You pause. "Okay, if you say so. We'll be on our way, then. Oh, actually. What's your name, good sir?"
"I'm Roy."

"Just a wandering mechanic."

All you wanted was a nice vacation.
You just wanted to take your partner and child to take a hike in the Wilds.
You didn't want to run into a bear. Particularly not one that's now chasing you---chasing your family---oh Silvanus, Epona, Cthulhu, whoever's out there, please save your family---

You trip over a branch. Your partner screams, but you call to them, 'Leave me! Keep going! Get away from here!'
As you struggle to your feet, you turn back to the bear, hoping to buy time for your family to escape. Your partner is hesitant, but for the sake of your child, they turn to flee towards a nearby shelter.
The bear reaches you, and you fight it as best as you can. It's no use.
You look to see your family one last time as you fade into unconsciousness. But it looks like they're... running back towards you?! No, that's... two other people...? You think?
Suddenly, a loud noise; the bear stumbles backwards. But it's too late. The last thing you see is a small bird zooming towards you from the direction of the pair.

You come to(?!) in a makeshift tent, a dull pain in your head along with everything else. A very strange imp floats before you. You manage to croak out, 'Is this Hell? I just wanted to protect my family... please, tell me they're safe.'
The imp laughs - you suppose it is an imp, after all, what did you expect. But as if summoned, an angel garbed in purple walks in---you blink a few times in surprise and your vision stabilises, it's just a short Grung woman holding a humanoid child. The woman speaks, 'How are you feeling? Your family is fine - they're at our shelter right now, but Kukudh will let them know you're awake.'
At that, the imp turns into a bird, and flies off. Your voice is hoarse, your thoughts confused, but you tell her about your pain, then ask, 'So... I'm not dead?'
She shakes her head. 'You're not. Your family encountered my husband and I in enough time that we were able to save you, though you'll likely have scars for life.' Seemingly absentmindedly, she rubs at a scar down the middle of her forehead. 'Consider it a reminder, I suppose.'
'But, the bear... did your husband kill it, then?' One of her eyes raises, and you feel... oddly scared. 'I-I mean, just, you don't look like the fighting t-type, you're so small, a-and---'
She stops you, and raises her robes to reveal gleaming mithral armour, and a holstered wooden revolver. 'Appearance isn't everything. I shot the bear, yes, but only to buy you time. My husband's been speaking with her to try and understand the situation.'

You can't help but look around in panic - the bear's here?! She tries to calm you down: 'Don't worry. She and her cub aren't intending to cause any harm, so long as you aren't. You're more alike than you think, you know.'
With that, a flap opens, and a bear---a smaller one?! There's two of them now?!---sticks its head into the room. You flinch in fear, but the Grung seems strangely unphased, even when the bear starts talking---wait, talking?!
'Hey, Sab, we got the situation figured out. She'd just like an apology from you for shooting at her, and our word that we'll act to prevent this happening again.'
The Grung - Sab? - nods, and pulls a lilac berry out of a pouch at her waist, bringing it over to you. 'Eat this, it'll help. Kukudh tells me your family will be here soon.' As you gladly take it, she leaves the tent, kissing the bear on the nose as she goes; it waits a moment, before seemingly judging (correctly) you'd be less nervous if it left and following her... 'Wait, is that bear her husband?'
`Yeah, what of it?` You didn't realise you spoke out loud, nor that the imp-pigeon-thing was back, your family in tow. You splutter for a moment in pure shock. 'I--- but--- he's twice her size---'
They laugh again, and grant you the mercy of finishing their sentence, `Roy's a shapeshifter, that's not his normal form. That expression on your face was great, though~`
As you blink rapidly, processing this information, the imp moves aside, and your partner and child rush into the tent to talk to you, and you're not sure if it's the pain, or the emotion, or the sheer weirdness of the situation, but you can't help but cry.

After a while, a loud noise shocks you out of your reunion. You struggle to your feet, worried about your saviours - it hurts, but far less than it really should... who ARE these people? No, that's something to worry about later, you think as you - supported by the surprisingly-strong imp and by your family - head to the tent flap to look outside.
You witness something you didn't expect. On one side, the she-bear which attacked you, a cub on her back. On the other - the smaller bear, the child, and the Grung woman. Both adult bears are digging a large hole; the woman seems to be commanding a hand made of water to move dirt aside.
As you watch, Sab nods, says something, and the bears step back; she makes a motion with her hands, and clean water begins to fill the pond, which the she-bear and cub drink from happily. The smaller bear, on the other hand, shimmers slightly as its---his---form changes into that of a humanoid man. A few bugs fly from his pocket to hand him a strange stone, which he starts to talk into. Nothing will surprise you any more, will it?

Sab notices you watching, smiles, and hops over. 'Alright, so... you went off the marked path, from the looks of it. Not too far off, not enough that it would be a problem under most circumstances, but you happened to run into her and her cub, who were also out of their normal roaming area due to a lack of water. Basically, she thought you were threatening her cub, and acted accordingly.'
'And then she... attacked us.' You can't help but sound a little bitter over that.
'Yes - to protect her cub. Wouldn't you do the same, fight to protect your family? Oh, yes, you did that.' She sounds a little stern, but reassuring. 'Anyway, that's where we came in. I shot in her general direction to draw attention, so that she would leave you alone, and Kukudh could get to you to stabilise you and channel my magic without getting killed themselves. I could bring you back from the dead in theory, but in practise, better to avoid that where possible - it's an exhausting process for everyone involved.'
...transforming? Channeling magic through an imp? Bringing people back from the dead?!
'My husband was then able to transform to talk to her, while I stayed to protect our child in the event of conflict. I'm glad it didn't come to it. We'd win, but I'd rather not fight if not necessary - especially when we understand her exact situation.'
She's so confident she could take on a bear, too... who are these people?
'Anyway, as you saw, we've made them a new pond. Roy's also talking with our friends at the City to hopefully raise awareness of keeping on the trail - they'd rather people stuck to the streets rather than go through their homes, why would wildlife be any different? As for you - you're free to go as soon as you feel better. Kukudh will stay with you until then, or fly back to the City to arrange transport. If you ever need anything, feel free to stop by Murry Hill.'

She's more perceptive than you thought... you weren't even aware your worry for your own fate was showing. 'I'm... thank you for being here, but... who are you...?' She smiles at your question.
'Just a wandering priestess of Sandigill, Warden of Waters. Your prayer to 'whoever's out there' reached him, you know - I got a sudden feeling we needed to go outside, and there you were.'
'...what can I---what can we do to repay you?'
'Respect life and nature, practise freedom and mercy. And do what you can with each day as it comes - you never know when it might be your last.' She bows, a little clumsily. 'Gil's blessings to you all.'

As she walks back to the man, you and your partner look at each other, and nod. You got a second chance at life today - it's time to put it to good use.
